_README: Label id -> structure name for the upper-arm MUSCLE volume derived from the Visible Human male colour cryosections by scripts/cryo/name_arm_muscles_from_cryo.py, plus the mapping onto atlas entities.

A KEY, not data. Geometry: the arm's muscle mass in the photographs, split by rules from standard anatomy (Gray's Anatomy 42nd ed.): posterior compartment = triceps brachii; anterior compartment within 22 mm of the humerus in the distal 65 % of the arm = brachialis; proximal 35 %, medial to the humerus and within 15 mm of it = coracobrachialis; the rest of the anterior compartment = biceps brachii. The boundaries between biceps and brachialis and around coracobrachialis are RULE-BASED, not traced along fascial planes; triceps is the most reliable (bounded by the septa and the humerus). Volumes (right/left): biceps 514/506, brachialis 164/221, coracobrachialis 44/50, triceps 713/789 cm3 -- the biceps is over-counted at the expense of brachialis by perhaps 100 cm3.
source: U.S. National Library of Medicine, The Visible Human Project (public domain), male colour cryosections, IDC series 4aaf9181-fb6a-4a4c-bf49-d1eb9ed4a385, registered to the CT (scripts/cryo/README.md). Rules: Standring S (ed.), Gray's Anatomy, 42nd ed., Elsevier 2021, 'Shoulder girdle and arm'.

biceps_right.note: superficial anterior compartment; boundary with brachialis rule-based

brachialis_right.note: anterior compartment within 22 mm of the humerus, distal 65 %

triceps_right.note: whole posterior compartment; three heads not separated

biceps_left.note: superficial anterior compartment; boundary with brachialis rule-based

brachialis_left.note: anterior compartment within 22 mm of the humerus, distal 65 %

triceps_left.note: whole posterior compartment; three heads not separated
